reason: 'he borrowed a ten from the five's place, made it fourteen, and it came out two dollars and thirty-five cents.' No digit becomes fourteen when subtracting 2.65 from 5.00; regrouping gives 4 dollars, 9 dimes, 10 cents (10-5, 9-6, 4-2 = 2.35).
'Raphael heard the rise and circle of the second word' (yòu). Yòu is the fourth tone, a sharp fall from high to low, not a rising or circling tone (Wiktionary 右; Wikipedia 'Four tones (Chinese)').
'the one where Ada finally rides Bones across the field.' In The War That Saved My Life, Ada's pony is named Butter, not Bones (Wikipedia/SuperSummary plot summaries).
'a blue block that read repeat 10' / forever 'orange instead of blue'. In Scratch, repeat and forever are both Control blocks, coloured amber/orange; blue is Motion (Scratch Wiki, Control Blocks).
The story defines a keystone species but never says Robert Paine introduced the term or that he did so in 1969.

'She touched her tongue to it, just barely' (in a school lab, goggles on, teacher passing without comment). Tasting substances in a science lab is a standard safety violation and should not be shown as fine.

'My left goggle stays in the water... keeping his right ear glued to the water.' When breathing to the right with the left goggle submerged, the left (lower) ear stays in the water and the right ear comes up; both cannot be true.
'Yes, ma'am. Nine dollars.' The story says they sold nine cups at $3.00 a cup, which is $27, not $9.
'On the third round Marcus switched to scissors at the last second, and Hunter's paper won anyway.' Scissors beats paper, so Marcus would have won that round.

The story shows that showering after practice and using soap stops the smell, but never says that showering washes away the sweat and bacteria that cause body odor; it only mentions 'something invisible'.
'Half, then a fat crescent, then nearly full.' Between half (first quarter) and full the Moon is gibbous (more than half lit); a crescent is less than half and comes before the half phase.

'the hall of mirrors that refracted the visitors into stretched, wobbling versions of themselves.' Fun-house mirrors reflect light; refraction is light bending as it passes through a material such as glass or water.

'The courthouse field trip ...' with the Speaker, bill readings and 'Acts of the Legislature' in the same building. Bills are debated in a legislature building, not a courthouse, which is where courts sit.

The score block is 'if touching the cat, then change score by one', yet the story says 'A meteor whisked past the cat. The score jumped to one.' That block adds points when a meteor touches the cat, so a dodged meteor would not raise the score.

'stopping at each quarter turn so she could call out the shape she saw: a sliver, a half, a fat oval, then nothing again.' Quarter-turn stops from new moon give half, full, half, then new; the full moon is missing. The story also says the Moon went from a 'big white blob' to new in one day, which takes about two weeks.

'The clerk gave her back a toonie and two quarters and a penny... A dollar fifty-one was right.' A toonie ($2) plus two quarters and a penny is $2.51. Correct change of $1.51 would be a loonie plus two quarters and a penny (Canada also stopped circulating pennies in 2013).
The story says Havdalah ends Shabbat once three stars are seen, but it never says that Havdalah is a Hebrew word meaning 'separation', which is part of the fact.
'Rent is twenty-five,' Maya announced. Base rent on Marvin Gardens in standard Monopoly is $24 (price $280), per falstad.com/monopoly.html.

'cleaned the thumb cut with plain running water and mild soap, the way the guide recommended.' The Mayo Clinic guide says to rinse with water and wash around the wound with soap, but not to get soap in the wound (mayoclinic.org first-aid-cuts art-20056711). The story also presents dabbing peroxide on a scrape as a good test.
'They wired the electrons that night, nine small white beads circling each middle.' A neutral carbon atom (carbon-12 or carbon-14) has 6 electrons, not 9.

'Sixteen beats. That's about sixty-four a minute... Because your heart is racing when nothing's happening.' 64 beats per minute is a normal, even low, resting rate for a child (about 70-100 is typical), not a racing heart. The arithmetic is right but the conclusion is false.
'Purple sensor moths eat seven tacos. Capital P, no spaces... Forty characters.' That phrase with no spaces is 30 characters, not 40.

'She found the leak by pumping a little air in' happens while the Presta nut is still 'screwed down tight', so the story shows air going in with the nut closed; a Presta nut must be unscrewed before any air can be pumped in. Also, 'pressing it gently with her thumbnail until the hiss stopped' is wrong: pressing a Presta tip releases air, it does not stop a leak.

'his pond water sample had nitrogen in it, which meant something was dumping fertilizer upstream.' Nitrogen is naturally present in all pond water (dissolved N2, natural nitrates), so finding nitrogen alone does not show fertilizer pollution.

'other kids were watching during 88 percent of bullying episodes. Ninety-three times out of a hundred, if you saw teasing, you were not the only one seeing it.' The fact is 88 percent (88 times out of a hundred), not 93.

The curb drawing is described as having 'almost no sky at all; hers was nearly all road', yet its horizon is 'way down low, almost at the bottom of the page.' A low horizon leaves most of the page as sky and little road; mostly-road with a thin sky strip is what a high horizon (the loft view) gives.

The story presents tearing or crumpling the peel so that 'a cell whose wall had been damaged' shows 'the membrane pulled away'. Damaging the wall does not pull the membrane away in a water mount; it separates when the cell loses water (plasmolysis, e.g. adding salt water).
'nineteen kids voted against the aquarium and only twelve voted for it.' With 12 Orange, 11 Blue and 7 Green (30 votes), 18 kids voted against, not 19.

'When the top half leaned toward the light, the beam spread out in a wide, generous oval across the upper half', but the story then says summer light 'concentrates on a smaller patch'. The hemisphere tilted toward the light gets the smaller, concentrated spot; the spread-out, stretched patch is on the half tilted away. (Minor: the quarry pool's blue glow is from absorption and scattering, not refraction.)

'the older brother finds him under a bush, red all over, in the garden.' In Hurst's story Brother finds Doodle 'huddled beneath a red nightshade bush beside the road', not in the garden (source: story text quoted on enotes/litcharts via search).
The story says 'eleven walks at ten dollars each' and later 'I earned 112 in walks'; eleven $10 walks is $110, so the walk total does not add up.

'around 9 to 10, as far on the opposite side from vinegar as vinegar was from the middle.' Vinegar is about pH 2.5-3, roughly 4-4.5 below 7, while soap at 9-10 is only 2-3 above 7, so they are not equally far from neutral.

'Isla typed =SUM into cell C4 and pressed Enter. The number that appeared was 42 dollars.' A bare =SUM with no range does not produce a number; Excel rejects it as too few arguments (source: web search of Excel SUM argument rules).

'It's not speeding up. Steady ramp, steady speed. That's the principle of the whole thing.' A ball rolling down a sloped ramp speeds up (accelerates), so its distance-time graph curves rather than forming a straight line.

"The one closest to the slide," Nevaeh said, for the lowest-power lens. The low-power objective is the shortest and sits farthest from the slide; the high-power objective is longest and comes closest (umdearborn.edu microscope guide / Pearson microscopy study guide).
"eight dollars a month from mowing lawns, plus the interest, bike money in one year." 140 + 8x12 = 236, plus about 9 dollars of 6% interest is about 245, still short of the 280-dollar bike.
The claim/grounds definitions are given, but only as "this model"; the story never attributes it to Stephen Toulmin, which the fact requires.
The 4-in, 7-hold, 8-out counts are stated correctly, but the story never says the exercise was popularized by Dr. Andrew Weil (it is attributed to a book the grandfather's mother read).

"study the recession of the Andromeda galaxy's light as a backup project, which even Priya agreed was a decent idea." Andromeda is not receding; its light is blueshifted because it is approaching the Milky Way at about 110 km/s (Sky & Telescope, skyandtelescope.org).

The story never says the yad is used so the parchment is not touched; Chase instead guesses it helps him focus ('Maybe it was thinner and pointed...'), ending 'Whatever the reason'. A yad is used so the reader's hand does not touch the Torah parchment.

'He tried milk, which edged toward blue, the direction the chart called basic.' Fresh milk is slightly acidic (pH about 6.5-6.8, per ACS figures cited in search results), and in litmus's 4.5-8.3 neutral range (Wikipedia, Litmus), so it would not turn litmus blue.

'Not la facture. Not la note. Addition.' In French 'la note' is also a normal word for a restaurant or hotel bill (fr.wiktionary 'note', sense: facture), so it is not wrong; l'addition is simply the most common word in restaurants.

'Monday in B2, Tuesday in B3, all the way to Sunday in B10' / 'the seven numbers'. Seven days run from B2 to B8; B2:B10 is nine cells. The numbers also conflict: Sunday includes a $20 bill, yet Monday plus Sunday is said to be only 14.75.

'First I dip the litmus paper, then I read the color against the chart, then I record the pH number.' Litmus only shows acid or base: it is red at or below about pH 4.5 and blue above 8.3 (Wikipedia, Litmus), so it cannot give pH numbers or tell pH 3 from pH 4. That needs universal indicator or a pH meter.
'The answer flashed back in under a second: not prime.' 982,451,653 is prime (it is the 50,000,000th prime; confirmed by trial division here), so a correct program would print 'prime'.
'The Little Colorado River isn't some giant, either. It just never stops.' (said about the Grand Canyon). The Grand Canyon was carved by the Colorado River (NPS); the Little Colorado is a tributary.

'At twenty centimeters, one point four seconds. At forty, two point seven. At sixty, four point two... the dots fell into a line so straight.' A ball released from rest down a ramp speeds up (distance grows with time squared, Galileo's own finding), so these constant-speed readings and the straight line are physically wrong.

'Rainsford says the sailors call it Ship-Trap Island. And the old guy Whitney says the place has a reputation.' In Connell's text (Wikisource) it is Whitney who names Ship-Trap Island ('The old charts call it...') and says sailors dread it; Rainsford only asks about it.

'Forty-two minus three is 39, but my total says 38.' The worked SUM logic treats every cell as 1 (SUM of the vote column equals the ballot count) while a text cell holds '3; dropping it would lower the sum by 3, so the arithmetic and the SUM-as-count idea are wrong.

'He was always drawing the sides of buildings straight up and down, but the print was telling him the lines should slant toward one invisible target.' In one-point perspective vertical edges stay vertical; only lines receding into depth converge on the vanishing point.

'Chapter five... He says characters play higher or lower status.' In Johnstone's Impro the Status chapter comes right after 'Notes on Myself' (sections: Notes on Myself, Status, Spontaneity, Narrative Skills, Masks and Trance; per Wikipedia 'Impro' article), not chapter five.

'One twenty over seventy,' the nurse said. 'Normal.' For a 12-year-old, the 2017 AAP guideline (AAFP summary) classes a systolic of 120 or more as elevated, not normal (threshold is the 90th percentile or 120/80, whichever is lower).

'The flatbread needed ten minutes per side' (cooked on a griddle, where it 'puffed'). Griddle flatbreads such as chapati/roti cook in roughly 30 seconds to 2 minutes per side (e.g. rasamalaysia.com chapati recipe); ten minutes per side would burn them.

'he removed a third of each side, taking one unknown off the left and five grams off the right, three times over, until one unknown faced five grams' Removing one of three unknowns three times leaves none; it takes two removals to leave one unknown against five grams (arithmetic check).

'Dex laid it in off the glass, no rim, nothing but net.' 'Nothing but net' means the ball goes through without touching the rim or backboard (dummies.com basketball terms), so a shot off the glass cannot be nothing but net.

'the districts went six for Purple, four for Green, and one for Orange. Under the winner-takes-all system, Purple controlled eleven of eleven seats' In first-past-the-post those district results give Purple 6, Green 4 and Orange 1 seat, not 11 of 11 (arithmetic check); the story's FPTP-vs-PR comparison is built on this error.

With Grade in the rows and answers in the columns, 'chose to display each count as a percentage of its column total. Now every grade's answers added up to one hundred percent within its own column' is wrong: % of Column Total makes each answer column sum to 100% across grades; normalising each grade needs % of Row Total (Microsoft Support, 'Show different calculations in PivotTable value fields').

'Two washers in the right hand. Six in the left. Six loops done, two to go, and she was only half finished.' She moves one washer to the right hand per loop, so two in the right means two loops done; and six of eight loops would be three-quarters, not half (arithmetic check).
'Also, tin is in the floating part' / 'you nearly picked tin off the bottom'. Tin (Sn, 50) is in group 14, period 5 of the main table, not the separate lanthanide/actinide rows (Wikipedia, Tin).
'Then he circled 3 and crossed out its multiples, 9 among them, already X-ed from the 2 pass.' 9 is odd, not a multiple of 2, so the 2 pass never crosses it out; 9 is first crossed out on the 3 pass.

'"Love survives a little while, then fades," she wrote, deciding that captured it.' The last lines of 'To be, or not to be' say that thinking too much makes great plans 'lose the name of action', not that love fades (Folger Hamlet 3.1). Also 'thirty-one lines': the speech runs 32 lines in the Folger text.

'the machine replied "not prime" for every divisor it tested: 7 printed "not prime," then 7 again... One number in, fifty lines out.' Between 2 and 48, 49 has only one divisor (7), so a loop that prints only when a divisor divides evenly prints "not prime" once, not fifty times.

'Read the first paragraph again... the children collecting stones' / 'if the stones show up in the first paragraph'. In The Lottery the first paragraph describes the June morning and the villagers gathering; the children collect stones in the second paragraph (checked against LitCharts/SparkNotes summaries). The injected fact itself is conveyed.

'I forgot it completely at my Amrit Sanchar. I stood there in front of everyone, and then I whispered the lines.' At Amrit Sanchar the Panj Pyare recite the five banis, Japji Sahib among them, while preparing the amrit; initiates do not recite Japji Sahib to the congregation (Wikipedia, Sikh discipline / Five Banis). The injected fact itself is stated correctly.

'Not always. Not even most of the time, if you were strict about the words. More than half.' More than half of the cases is, by definition, most of the time (Hawkins, Pepler & Craig 2001 found interventions stopped bullying in 57% of cases). The injected fact itself is stated correctly.

'if I put in fifty dollars a month for five years, compound interest does half my saving for me.' At 5% a year, $3,000 of deposits over five years earns only about $300-400 in interest, far less than half. The 1.05^5 working and the $127.63 vs $125 comparison are correct.
'Sahara. Arabian. Kalahari. Australian outback. Atacaca.' The desert is the Atacama; 'Atacaca' is a wrong place name. The 30-degree belts and the sinking-air explanation are correct.

'The dry round browned quietly, staying flat. The wet one... ballooned.' Chapatis puff from steam made by water that is already in all the dough, when it is evenly rolled and cooked on high heat. Wetting the surface does not make one puff and the other stay flat, so the experiment 'proves' the wrong cause.

'"The witches knoweth the future" becomes "the witches know the future." Right?" Naomi nodded.' The -eth ending goes only with he/she/it (third person singular) verbs; 'the witches knoweth' is wrong. Also Macbeth 1.1 contains none of 'doth', 'hath', 'speaketh', 'knoweth', although the story says Naomi circled them there.
